title: The Uncharted Canopy Where Growth Reads Itself

features.name: sprouting-ferns-documentary
features.desc-on-touch: Young ferns uncurl here—each frond a record of unrolling. The archive has placed sensors that measure the unfurling in millimetres. Growth *speaks*. You are watching the forest read its own becoming in real time.

features.name: sapling-height-markers
features.desc-on-touch: Notches carved into young trunks, dates carved beside them: 2018, 2020, 2022. The trees are measuring their own rise. The archive didn't impose this—the forest discovered that growth leaves a legible trail if you're patient enough to read it.

features.name: leaf-fall-weaving-pattern
features.desc-on-touch: Leaves have accumulated in mathematical precision—not by human hand, but by the forest's own intention. The pattern suggests a textile, a weave-map of seasons layering downward. The canopy is stitching itself into the earth.

features.name: root-surface-mapping
features.desc-on-touch: Where soil has eroded, roots rise to the surface in sculptured relief. The archive has photographed them, overlaid them with contour maps. The tree's roots are a topography. The ground learns its own shape by being roots.

features.name: canopy-gap-light-study
features.desc-on-touch: A shaft of light penetrates the leaves, illuminating nothing but air and dust. The archive has timed this—nine minutes a day, only in late afternoon. The gap itself is a text. The trees are writing with sunlight.
